title: Investigation Bootcamp: KV Warmth Metric Catalog & Tracing Primer
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, hands-on kit for an internal "investigation bootcamp" focused on KV cache "warmth" and fast-path vs slow-path token latency. The goal is to give operators and on-call engineers a small metric catalog, trace annotation guidance, and dashboard recipes they can use during live drills and postmortems.

Context and why this matters:
- KV cache warmth (fraction of requests that hit a warmed KV prefix state) is a dominant driver for P50->P99 token latency in our multi-tenant serving runtime.
- Observability gaps: historically we had coarse kvcache-hit metrics at pool level but lacked per-session prefix-tagging and trace anchors that show prefetch vs on-demand paths.
- This bootcamp emphasizes reproducible investigation steps and a minimal metric set to avoid query cost explosions during debugging.

Audience:
- Newer oncall engineers (SRE rotation)
- Engineers owning model rollouts and rollout dashboards
- Solutions and customer-facing engineers who need to explain latency root cause to customers

Quick TL;DR metric catalog (minimal, cost-aware) - each metric below should have consistent names and units:
1) inference.requests.total (counter) - total API requests by model/version/route
2) inference.tokens.generated (counter) - generated tokens, partition by model, sequence_length_bucket
3) kv.warmth.session_fraction (gauge, 0..1) - fraction of user sessions whose initial prefix warm state was found; tag by model, tenant_id_cohort
4) kv.prefetch.rate (counter/sec) - number of proactive prefetch operations issued per pool
5) kv.evict.rate (counter/sec) - eviction events per pool (helps correlate warm->cold spikes)
6) latency.first_token_ms (histogram) - time to first token from request arrival, with histogram buckets tuned to 5/20/50/100/300/1000 ms
7) latency.token_step_ms (histogram) - per-token generation latency (use delta between token emission timestamps)
8) route.fallback.count (counter) - counts of policy-driven fallbacks (e.g., model variant fallback)
9) trace.sampled.true_ratio (gauge) - ratio of requests that reached full-span sampling vs minimal header traces
10) investigation.cost.queries_per_min (gauge) - a lightweight guard metric that tracks diagnostic query rate from dashboards to avoid runaway investigation cost

Definitions and tagging conventions (short):
- tenant_id_cohort: hashed low-cardinality bucket (high/med/low) to avoid exposing PII and to control cardinality.
- model_version: short tag (e.g., gptx-7b-v1) used for rollouts.
- session_id: ephemeral, only included in traces and short-lived logs; do NOT export to long-term metrics.
- prefix_category: 'short-prompt' | 'long-prompt' | 'system-heavy' (used for sampling/observability slice)

Trace/span annotation primer (for investigation effectiveness):
- Root span: request.receive -> annotate with route, model_version, tenant_cohort, sequence_length_bucket
- KV check span (kv.check) - include attributes: prefix_hint, cache_hit=true|false, prefetch_triggered=true|false, kvcache_latency_ms
- Model enqueue span (runtime.enqueue) - attributes: pool_id, gpu_instance_type, batch_size_enqueued
- Model compute span (runtime.compute) - attributes: kernel_variant, quant_mode, kv_cache_used=true|false
- Response assembly span (runtime.assemble) - attributes: tokens_emitted, partial_streaming_sent
- Error spans - attach error.code and error.count and ensure partial traces are still linkable via request_id

Sampling strategy notes (practical):
- Default: lightweight headers-only traces for all requests containing request_id, model, tenant_cohort (keeps cardinality low).
- Full capture: 1% baseline plus boosted sampling for requests where kv.check.cache_hit=false AND latency.first_token_ms > 100 ms.
- Rollout captures: during model rollouts, lift full-capture sampling to 5% for affected model_version + 100% capture for a tiny percentage (0.1%) of tenants in the rollout ring for deep dives.

Dashboard recipe (operator-first, low-query-cost):
1) Landing panel: P50, P90, P99 latency.first_token_ms by model_version (heatmap sparkline).
2) KV Warmth overview: kv.warmth.session_fraction by tenant_cohort and pool_id (stacked bar, 6h/24h).
3) Prefetch vs on-demand: kv.prefetch.rate vs kv.check.cache_hit rate (line chart).
4) Trace sampling gauge: trace.sampled.true_ratio with annotation overlays when sampling policy changed.
5) Investigator mini-dashboard (hidden by default): shows top 10 request_ids with full traces (only populated when user triggers 'deep-dive mode') and investigation.cost.queries_per_min meter to throttle queries.

Investigation playbook (steps during a live incident):
- Step 0: quiet start - snapshot global metrics (requests, tokens, kv.warmth.session_fraction) and note the time window.
- Step 1: check pool-level throttles and pool latency histograms (if many pools show elevated first_token latency, likely infra or common prefetch regressions).
- Step 2: open the KV Warmth overview and identify tenant_cohort with sharp drops; if cohort-level drop -> check prefetch.rate and evict.rate.
- Step 3: enable boosted trace capture for the affected model_version + tenant_cohort (follow sampling policy; keep duration bounded to 10–20 minutes).
- Step 4: pick representative request_ids (use the investigator mini-dashboard) and follow KV check spans -> look for common attributes: prefix_category, prefetch_triggered=false, kvcache_latency_ms large.
- Step 5: triage: if kvcache_latency_ms high but prefetchs low, suspect prefetch scheduler backlog; if prefetch high but cache_hit still low, suspect eviction pressure or prefix mismatch.
- Step 6: mitigation options (fast): temporarily raise prefetch.rate for affected pool(s), scale dedicated pools, or rollback a rollout that changed prefix heuristics.

On-call table-top exercise (bootcamp activity):
- 30-minute scenario: sudden P99 increase for multi-tenant endpoint serving gptx-7b-v1.
- Teams: operator, infra, runtime, solutions.
- Tasks: reproduce the timeline using metrics, enable trace captures, identify 3 candidate root causes, propose an immediate mitigation.
- Debrief: what logs/traces were missing? what metric would have shortened time-to-root-cause?

Dashboard cost and safety guidance (do this always):
- Do not enable full-trace capture for more than 15 minutes across whole fleet. Use cohort and model filters.
- investigator mini-dashboard must require a permission flag and rate-limit all query-driven trace expands.
- Add a circuit-breaker metric (investigation.cost.queries_per_min) and alert quietly if > threshold.

SLO mapping (how these metrics feed SLOs):
- user-facing SLO: request.successful && latency.first_token_ms < 300 ms (target: 99.5% for paid tier). Map to a derived metric slo.first_token_300ms_ratio.
- infra SLO: kv.warmth.session_fraction > 0.75 for 95% of the time on healthy pools.

Open questions / unresolved decisions (for bootcamp discussion):
- How to represent multi-prefix sessions where partial warmth exists? Proposal: prefix_warmth_vector sampling in traces but not in metrics (too high-cardinality).
- Should prefetch be per-tenant or centralized per-pool? Ops cost tradeoffs need a small experiment.
- Exact histogram bucketization for token_step_ms needs a calibration run across short/medium/long prompts.

Next steps & action items:
- [Aisha] Draft instrumentation PR with metric names and required tags (due 2026-01-20) -> linked PR stub in GitHub.
- [Ravi] Build the investigator mini-dashboard mock and implement the queries with a query budget guard (due 2026-01-28).
- [Emily] Create the tabletop scenario in runbook repo and schedule bootcamp (2 sessions: Jan and Feb).
- [Noah] Run calibration job for token_step_ms bucketization and report back with recommended buckets (due 2026-01-18).

Appendix: quick references and snippets
- Low-cost trace header example (pseudo):
  X-Trace-Minimal: request_id={{rid}};model={{model}};tenant_cohort={{cohort}}
- Full capture trigger rule (pseudo):
  IF kv.check.cache_hit==false AND latency.first_token_ms > 100ms -> set sample=1
- Recommended dashboard query guard: queries_per_min < 50 for investigator dashboards by default

Notes to self (bootcamp instructor tips):
- Emphasize experiment-driven metrics: start small, measure query cost, iterate.
- Keep language low-cardinality and privacy-safe.
- Use real tickets from past incidents as scenario seeds (easier for learners).

If you want I can convert the metric list into a Prometheus exposition format and draft the initial instrumentation PR text for runtime owners.
